summary: The agent implemented a broad, legitimate seedable-lazy feature and preserved all baseline behavior, but 2 of 13 new tests failed because an already explicitly seeded hybrid with-method always constructs a new immutable instance instead of returning the same instance when the supplied seed is equal.
quick_failure_summary: Hybrid with-methods do not retain instance identity when given a value equal to an existing explicit seed.

details.reasoning: The implementation's generated seedable-lazy with-methods route every supplied value through returnSeededLazyCopy, which builds a new object without first checking whether the attribute is already explicitly seeded with an equal value. This causes both failing assertions: withScalar(computedFallback) correctly creates a distinct explicitly seeded value from a merely computed fallback, but calling withScalar(computedFallback) again on that explicitly seeded value should return the same instance; likewise, withNumber(OptionalInt.empty()) on an object already explicitly seeded with OptionalInt.empty() should return the same instance. The reference implementation preserves the crucial distinction by applying the normal wither equality optimization only when seedableLazyIsSeeded is true.
details.secondary_factors: The agent added extensive legitimate fixture coverage, but its own tests checked seed preservation and replacement rather than the established same-instance behavior for equal wither values.

justification.issue_description: Generated hybrid with-methods fail to return this when the hybrid already has an explicit seed equal to the requested value, while still needing to create a new explicitly seeded object when only an equal computed fallback exists.
justification.evidence: The prompt explicitly distinguishes an equal computed fallback, stating that calling a hybrid with-method with such a value must establish an explicit seed. Existing Immutables.generator with-method implementations repeatedly use equality checks followed by return this, and existing visible tests such as ValuesTest.java lines 627-629 and WithEnumsTest.java lines 36-44 assert same-instance behavior for equal values. Therefore the expected hybrid rule was inferable: bypass the equality shortcut for unseeded/computed state, but preserve it for an equal explicit seed.
justification.verdict_reasoning: FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT is appropriate because the exact same-instance sentence was not written verbatim in the prompt, but preserving ordinary generated with-method semantics was clearly foreseeable from the surrounding generator and existing tests. The agent implemented the special computed-fallback seeding rule but omitted the seed-state-guarded equality optimization rather than encountering an undocumented hidden-only expectation.

problem_assessment.notes: This is a large cross-cutting annotation-processor feature involving builders, withers, copy provenance, modifiables, exceptions, serialization, marshaling, and validation. The prompt is unusually detailed, and the only failed expectation also follows established visible with-method conventions. The reference solution demonstrates that the task is solvable.

evidence: JUnit reports show all 326 baseline tests passed and 11 of 13 new tests passed; both new failures are ordinary assertion failures in generated with-method behavior.
The trajectory shows focused tests, processor tests, and the full fixture suite completed successfully in the solve-time environment.
The agent reached a completed implementation and final review; there were no dependency, permission, runtime, network, API, or bootstrap failures that prevented work.
Although the post-agent log records a failed 3-way test.patch merge attempt, the harness recovered and executed all 13 new tests, so it did not cause or obscure the two behavioral failures.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the verifier exercised the implementation and exposed a localized wither identity omission.
